claim: On 8x RTX 3090 over PCIe 4.0 x16 with BAR1 P2P enabled, NCCL all-reduce bus bandwidth reaches 24.7 GB/s versus 2.7 GB/s on NCCL's no-P2P SHM transport, a 9x collective-fabric jump.
stance_target: cc-6's committed reading that P2P is a latency lever, not a bandwidth lever — this shows P2P IS a bandwidth lever when BAR1 covers the framebuffer and the link is wide
scope_conditions: 8x RTX 3090 (GA102), EPYC Rome, four root complexes, PCIe 4.0 x16, BAR1 resized to cover the 24 GB framebuffer, patched open kernel modules + stock 610.57.04 userspace
quoted_support: Under the hood: direct peer copies run at **23-26 GB/s** across the root complex (PCIe 4.0 x16 line rate) versus ~2 GB/s per GPU through host staging, and NCCL all-reduce bus bandwidth reaches **24.7 GB/s** versus 2.7 GB/s on NCCL's no-P2P SHM transport — a 9x collective-fabric jump

claim: BAR1 P2P requires static BAR1 to span the whole framebuffer, so BAR1 must be resized (32 GB on a 3090, 64 GiB on an unlocked CMP 170HX) before the GH100 BAR1-P2P HAL check can pass.
stance_target: the mechanism by which the 170HX's stock 64 MB BAR1 blocks BAR1 P2P, and why the memory unlock's 64 GiB BAR1 is the enabling step
scope_conditions: NVIDIA open kernel modules, kbusIsPcieBar1P2PMappingSupported_GH100, static BAR1
quoted_support: static BAR1 (and therefore BAR1 P2P) requires BAR1 to cover the whole framebuffer. ... BAR1 must end up covering the whole framebuffer (32 GB on a 3090). This is not cosmetic: BAR1-P2P maps peer memory

claim: The stock 610 driver already ships native BAR1 P2P for supported chips and needs no userspace changes; the fork only forces the GH100 BAR1-P2P HALs onto consumer chips that lack them.
stance_target: whether BAR1 P2P on a 170HX requires a bespoke userspace stack (it does not)
scope_conditions: open kernel modules 610 branch, stock 610.57.04 userspace
quoted_support: No userspace changes: the modules pair with the stock 610.57.04 userspace

claim: The 9x P2P bandwidth ratio is measured on GA102/AD102 at PCIe 4.0 x16 and does not transfer to a GA100 at Gen2 x4, where the link itself caps busbw near 1.6 GB/s.
stance_target: the scope limit of this counter-evidence for cc-6
scope_conditions: consumer Ampere/Ada at Gen4 x16 vs GA100 at Gen2 x4
